transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… I’m here because I can’t seem to keep things in order at work anymore. Tickets, receipts, notes, customer jobs—they all end up piled together, and then I don’t know what to deal with first.
Has this kind of trouble organizing and keeping track of things been a pattern for you since you were a child, or is this something new that started more recently?

It’s not really new. I mean… even back in grade school, teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but kind of scattered. I’d lose papers, talk when I wasn’t supposed to, and I needed reminders to actually finish my work.
Besides the trouble staying organized and focused, do you often feel restless, fidgety, or find it hard to sit still, or act impulsively without thinking things through?

Yeah… I guess I do that some. In church committee meetings, or those fabric-care trainings at work, I keep needing to get up—like for water, or papers, or to check something. Everybody else can just sit there, but I… I don’t seem to stay put very well.
Do you notice these same problems with organization, restlessness, or impulsivity affecting other parts of your life, like at home or in social situations, not just at work?

Yes… it’s not just work. At the shop, it’s caused late orders and mix-ups with billing, and there’ve been some… uncomfortable moments with staff and customers.

And at church, I’ve had to step back from leading some planning things, because people were getting frustrated with how I was handling it.

Thinking back to before you turned 12, can you recall specific examples where this restlessness or disorganization actually caused problems for you—like at home or in school—not just that teachers noticed you were 'scattered'?

I don’t remember every detail, but… yes. In grade school it caused trouble. Teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but I was always losing papers, talking when I shouldn’t, and needing reminders to finish my work. It wasn’t just them noticing—it did get me in trouble some.
Have you been feeling unusually sad, anxious, or worried recently, in a way that might be affecting your concentration or energy levels?
I don’t know… not unusually, I guess. I get worried about things sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it as the reason I can’t concentrate. It feels more like… that’s just how I am.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing much more than normal?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have busy days where I’m wound up, but not several days like that… not needing sleep or anything.
Do you currently use alcohol, recreational drugs, or any medications that might affect your concentration or energy levels?
Not really… I mean, nothing I can think of that would explain it. I don’t use drugs. Alcohol… not much. And I’m not on anything that I’ve noticed makes me foggy or wired.
